subject: Optimizing timer() and ggspectro() parameters - odd behavior

messages.author: c5de8c8c086d2efe
messages.subject: Optimizing timer() and ggspectro() parameters - odd behavior
parts:
Dear all, 

I'm using the timer() function to detect bat calls in my recordings. I'm having an issue with the parameter settings and wanted to ask for some advice regarding both the optimization of timer() and plotting parameters for ggspectro(). 

Problem:
My recordings were made in a sound-isolated chamber - so there's relatively little noise. For a given file, I will get pretty good identification of most calls, but then for some sections of the very same file there are tons of detections of simple noise and they are plotted as though noise is exceptionally high. Since the noise level is pretty uniform within each recording (~1 minute each), I don't quite understand this behavior. 

My questions are:
1. Is the amplitude threshold in timer() relative to the whole file, or just the current sliding window? 
2. Why would timer() identify calls from noise correctly in one section of the file and catch many false positives in another, if the energy levels are about the same?
3. Theoretically, what's the best strategy to detect calls using timer() if noise levels do vary within a single file? 
4. Are the limits/colevels parameters in the ggspectro/spectro functions scaled to the rms or energy of the selected sample?

Sample Data & Output:
Below you will find my pipeline. Here you will also find an example sound file and the plotted spectrograms and detected calls output by the program below: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XMWspiV10mWUT4WrmXBAqq527N3Sr__e?usp=sharing
As you can see, some sections of the sound file are plotted by ggspectro as though background noise is very high, while other sections seem 'cleaner'. But if you open the sound file in a software like Audacity or Avisoft, there's not much difference. (E.g. minute 8.2-8.4 has an rms of -65.16 while the section 9-9.2 min has an rms of -65.19. But looking at the spectrograms plotted (file02_8 and file02_9, respectively), it appears as though the latter has much more noise and there are a ton of false positives.)

Pipeline: 
# filter each sound file to desired freq range
wav.filt <- seewave::ffilter(wav@left, f = w...@samp.rate, from = 10000, to = 120000)

# get call data 
call_data <- seewave::timer(wav.filt, f=w...@samp.rate, 
                threshold = 1, 
                dmin = 0.001,
                envt = 'abs', 
                power = 1, 
                msmooth = c(512,50), # window, overlap
                plot = FALSE)

# in case a call starts right at the end of the file but an end is not recorded, assume it ends at the end of the file and set the offset value 

    if (length(call_data$s.start) > length(call_data$s.end) & 
        dplyr::last(call_data$s.end)<dplyr::last(call_data$s.start)) {
        call_data$s.end <- c(call_data$s.end,length(wav@left)/w...@samp.rate)
        }

# weld into df and quantify onset intervals between calls

    calls <- data.frame(sig.start = call_data$s.start, sig.end = call_data$s.end) %>%
                        dplyr::rename(starts = sig.start,
                                      ends = sig.end) %>%
                        mutate(duration = call_data$s,
                               onset.interval = starts-dplyr::lag(starts)) %>%
                        mutate(min = filenum, .before = 1) 

# plot the spectrogram of the file along with detected calls to ensure correct detections:

 checker <- calls[order(calls$starts),] %>% add_column(y.val = 95)
      graph.path <- file.path(results_path,'graphical_check')
        dir.create(graph.path,recursive = TRUE)

# plot in segments because 1 minute is way too long to see the details:
      segments <- seq(from = 0, to = length(wav@left)/w...@samp.rate, length.out = 50)

      for (i in 2:length(segments)) {
        curr_seg <- checker %>% dplyr::filter(min==as.character(filenum))
        curr_seg <-  curr_seg[which(curr_seg$starts<=segments[i] & curr_seg$starts>segments[i-1]), ]
        if (!nrow(curr_seg)==0) {
        seewave::ggspectro(wav.filt, 
             tlim = c(segments[i-1],segments[i]), 
             f = w...@samp.rate,
             wl = 512, ovlp = 50, 
fastdisp = TRUE, palette = temp.colors,
                    noisereduction = TRUE)  + 
                    geom_tile(mapping = aes(fill = amplitude)) +
                    geom_segment(data = curr_seg,
 mapping = aes(x = starts, y = y.val,                                                 xend = ends, yend = y.val,
                     color = "red"),                            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2) +
                  scale_fill_continuous(name="Amplitude\n(dB)\n", limits=c(-70,0),
                    na.value="transparent", low="white", high="black") +
                    theme_bw() +
                    ggsave(file.path(graph.path,paste0('file',filenum,'_',i,'.png'))) }


Thank you so much in advance!
Ava

messages.subject: Re: Optimizing timer() and ggspectro() parameters - odd behavior
parts:
Dear Jerome & others, 

I've implemented a version of the timer() function that operates directly on the envelope. I think this may be helpful for some if, as in my case, one has to first manipulate the envelope outside of the timer() function. 

My amendment also allows you to supply an exact value for the threshold. (In timer(), the threshold argument can either be a function or a percentage of the max amplitude. However, if the threshold that you want to use is known, this can be supplied.)

```
# Fixes by Yannick Jadoul implemented here
# https://groups.google.com/g/seewave/c/UkEeyixxjV4

env_timer <- function(file.env, 
                      f, 
                      threshold = 1,
                      thresholding = "percent", # "percent" - % amplitude (if max amplitude == 1), 
                                                # "apply" - use the exact value given, 
                      dmin = 0.001,
                      power = 1, 
                      tlim = NULL,
                      plot = FALSE,
                      tplot = NULL) # provide the section you want to view 
  
{
  
# Checks -------------------------------
  if (is.null(file.env))
    stop("envelope missing")
  env <- file.env
  n <- length(env)
  if (is.null(f))
    stop("sampling rate missing")
  f <- f
  t <- seq(0,n/f,length.out=n)
  if (!is.null(dmin)) {
    if (length(dmin) != 1) 
      stop("'dmin' should be a numeric vector of length 1")
    if (dmin <= 0) 
      stop("'dmin' cannot be negative or equal to 0")
    if (dmin >= n/f) 
      stop("'dmin' cannot equal or be higher than the wave duration")
  }
  if (power == 0) 
    stop("'power' cannot equal to 0")

  
# Segment in time? -------------------------------
  if (!is.null(tlim)) {
    env <- env[seq(tlim[1]*f,tlim[2]*f)]
    t <- t[seq(tlim[1]*f,tlim[2]*f)]
    n <- length(env)
  } else if (!is.null(tlim) & !length(tlim)==2) {
    stop("incorrect number of arguments to 'tlim'")
  }

# Thresholding -------------------------------
  if (thresholding == "apply") {
    thres <- threshold
  } else if (thresholding == "percent" && is.numeric(threshold)) {
    thres <- threshold/100
  } else if (is.function(threshold)) {
    thres <- apply(wave1, MARGIN = 2, FUN = threshold)
  }
  
# Power ------------------------------- 
  if (power != 1) {
    env[which(env<0)] <- 0
    env1 <- env^power
  } else {
    env1 <- env}
  
# Plot --------------------------------
  if (plot) {
    if (!is.null(tlim)) {
      p <- plot(t,env1,type = "l",xlab = "seconds", ylab = "Amplitude (a.u.)")
        abline(h = thres, col = "red", lty = 2)
        mtext(paste(as.character(round(thres,digits = 3)), "%"), side = 2, line = 0.5, at = thres, 
              las = 1, col = "red", cex = 0.8)
    } else if (!is.null(tplot)) {
      p <- plot(t[seq(tplot[1]*f,tplot[2]*f)],env1[seq(tplot[1]*f,tplot[2]*f)],type = "l", xlab = "seconds", 
                ylab = "Amplitude (a.u.)")
      abline(h = thres, col = "red", lty = 2)
      mtext(paste(as.character(round(thres,digits = 3)), "%"), side = 2, line = 0.5, at = thres, 
          las = 1, col = "red", cex = 0.8)
    } else {
      p <- plot(t,env1,type = "l", xlab = "seconds", 
                ylab = "Amplitude (a.u.)")
      abline(h = thres, col = "red", lty = 2)
      mtext(paste(as.character(round(thres,digits = 3)), "%"), side = 2, line = 0.5, at = thres, 
            las = 1, col = "red", cex = 0.8)
    }
    print(p)
  }
  # Filtering for values above threshold  -------------------------------
  env2 <- ifelse(env1 <= thres, yes = 1, no = 2) # 1 = below thresh, 2 = above thresh
  env3 <- (env2+dplyr::lead(env2))[-length(env2)] # 2 = silent, 3 = transitions, 4 = signal
  n3 <- length(env3) # because the lead addition removes the final sample
  env3[c(1, n3)] <- 3 
  env4 <- which(env3 == 3)  
  
# Filtering for values above dmin  -------------------------------
  if (!is.null(dmin)) {
    event.dur <- diff(env4)
    event.idx <- which(event.dur < dmin * f)
    if (length(event.idx) != 0) {
      for (i in event.idx) {
        env3[(env4[i]):(env4[i] + event.dur[i])] <- 2
      }
      env3[which(abs(diff(env3)) == 2)] <- 3 # if a transition has been removed, reinsert
      env3[c(1, n3)] <- 3
    }
    env4 <- which(env3 == 3) 
    if (length(env4) == 2) {
      stop("No calls detected. Was 'dmin' or 'threshold' set to too high a value?")
    }
  }
  env4[-1] <- env4[-1] + 1 # removes the first index and shifts all by 1 sample
  env3 <- ts(env3, start = 0, end = n3/f, frequency = f)
  positions <- time(env3)[env4] 
  durations <- diff(positions)
  npos <- length(positions)
  if (npos <= 2) 
    stop("It seems that the sound is continuous, there are no signal/pause events.")
  
 if (env2[1] == 1) {
#  if (env3[2] == 1) { # Edit by Yannick Jadoul
    first <- "pause"
    pause <- durations[seq(1, npos - 1, by = 2)]
    signal <- durations[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
    start.signal <- positions[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
    end.signal <- positions[seq(3, npos - 1, by = 2)] 
#    end.signal <- positions[seq(3, npos, by = 2)] # Edit by Yannick Jadoul
    } else {
    first <- "signal"
    pause <- durations[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
    signal <- durations[seq(1, npos - 1, by = 2)]
    start.signal <- positions[seq(1, npos - 1, by = 2)]
    end.signal <- positions[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
#    end.signal <- positions[seq(2, npos, by = 2)] # Edit by Yannick Jadoul
}
  
  # -- 
  if (length(start.signal) > length(end.signal)) {
    end.signal <- c(end.signal,n3/f)
    print("Added end signal.")
    flush.console()
  } else if (length(start.signal) < length(end.signal)) {
    stop("There's an extra end signal - investigate.")
  }
  
  
  ratio <- sum(signal)/sum(pause)
  timer <- list(s = signal, p = pause, r = ratio, s.start = start.signal, 
                s.end = end.signal, first = first)
  return(timer)
}

```


Thanks!
Ava

```
  if (length(start.signal) > length(end.signal)) {
    end.signal <- c(end.signal,n3/f)
    print("Added end signal.")
    flush.console()
  } else if (length(start.signal) < length(end.signal)) {
    stop("There's an extra end signal - investigate.")
  }
  
  
  ratio <- sum(signal)/sum(pause)
  timer <- list(s = signal, p = pause, r = ratio, s.start = start.signal, 
                s.end = end.signal, first = first)
  return(timer)
}

```


Thanks!
Ava

Dear all, 

I'm using the timer() function to detect bat calls in my recordings. I'm having an issue with the parameter settings and wanted to ask for some advice regarding both the optimization of timer() and plotting parameters for ggspectro(). 

Problem:
My recordings were made in a sound-isolated chamber - so there's relatively little noise. For a given file, I will get pretty good identification of most calls, but then for some sections of the very same file there are tons of detections of simple noise and they are plotted as though noise is exceptionally high. Since the noise level is pretty uniform within each recording (~1 minute each), I don't quite understand this behavior. 

My questions are:
1. Is the amplitude threshold in timer() relative to the whole file, or just the current sliding window? 
2. Why would timer() identify calls from noise correctly in one section of the file and catch many false positives in another, if the energy levels are about the same?
3. Theoretically, what's the best strategy to detect calls using timer() if noise levels do vary within a single file?

Hi Louise, 

My apologies for the very late reply - I somehow never got a notification of your comment. 

I also have experienced high computation times for sure (although I thought it simply had to do with the enormous amount of data I had to pass through this function), and I believe it has to do with the line:
```

```
since I can't see any other place where the script substantially diverges from the original in terms of functions called. 

Incidentally, I think this is also where the (more minor) bottleneck occurs in the original, where the signal/pause/transitions are computed with:
```
## 2 = silence, 3 = change, 4 = signal
n2 <- length(wave2)
wave4 <- apply(as.matrix(1:(n2-1)), 1, function(x) wave2[x] + wave2[x+1])
```

I don't recall anymore why I changed this to use dplyr, since they're equivalent commands and certainly using base R here would be faster. 

I'll take another look and post an updated version. I was just revisiting some suggestions made by @YannickJadoul on the timer() function, which I might also incorporate. 

Best,
Ava
